findings.title: The editorial seed command has no production guard and changes admin access, live articles and comments under real users' names.
findings.scenario: An operator runs the seed command on the live server, maybe after copying it from a setup note. If the hard-coded author emails do not exist, the very first account in the database (for example Tom) silently becomes a full content administrator, with publishing, invitation and moderation powers. Live launch guides are overwritten with localhost cover images, and made-up 'news' plus sample comments and reactions are posted under real members' accounts. Readers see fake regulatory news and comments that real pharmacists never wrote.
findings.test_needed: Run seed_editorial_content with production settings (DEBUG off, not public_hub.test_settings) and assert that it raises CommandError and makes no ContentAdministrator, Article or Comment changes.

owner_question.question: If someone runs the editorial seed command on the live site, what should happen to Tom's account, the published guides and the comments shown to readers?
options: Refuse to run outside local/test settings, like the hub preview seed
Allow it on live only with an explicit --i-know flag, and never grant admin or post comments as real users

findings.title: After a board report is resolved, the same user can never report that talent post or job shift again, yet is told the report was received.
findings.scenario: Sara reports a job board shift Tom posted, and a moderator resolves it without hiding it. Tom later edits the shift description into something abusive. When Sara reports it again she sees 'Report received', but the system only finds her old resolved report, so nothing new reaches the moderators.
findings.test_needed: Create a BoardReport by Sara, mark it resolved, have Sara POST the report again, and assert that an unresolved report now appears in the moderation queue.

owner_question.question: Sara's report on a job shift was dismissed, and the shift then changed. When she reports it again, what should happen?
options: A new open report reaches the moderators
Sara's old report reopens with her new reason
Keep today's behaviour (silently ignored, but she is told it was received)
